original_test_intent: Physically operate the PSU service handle and its associated latch/retention mechanism to verify correct fit, travel, engagement, release and user serviceability for the specified power-supply assembly.
original_method: An engineer examines and actuates the PSU handle, records photographs and judges mechanical accuracy. The source does not state that the PSU must be electrically removed or hot-swapped, so this review does not add either action.
manual_activity: The engineer must observe handle alignment, full travel, latch engagement and release, retention, abnormal free play or resistance, and any contact with the PSU bay or chassis. A remote agent cannot apply or sense the required force and cannot verify that the retention mechanism is mechanically secure.
required_inputs: PSU model, bay and handle/latch identity
Applicable chassis/PSU mechanical drawing or service specification
Approved state for handle actuation, including whether the PSU remains installed, de-energized or isolated
Acceptance limits for travel, retention, alignment, interference, force and visible damage
Qualified operator and photo/checklist evidence plan
safety_requirements: Do not treat handle actuation as authorization to release or remove an energized PSU.
Confirm redundant-power state, connector exposure and platform service procedure before any action that could unlatch the supply.
Use required ESD and pinch-point controls and support the PSU if the handle can disengage retention.
Stop on binding, cracking, failed lock, excessive play, interference, connector movement or an unexpected PSU/BMC event.
Do not force, repair or repeatedly cycle the handle after an anomaly.
Do not clear SEL, kernel or BMC evidence for this mechanical inspection.
agent_execution_scope: Prepare a PSU-handle inspection checklist tied to the supplied drawing/specification.
Organize engineer-supplied before, engaged, released and restored-state photographs.
Correlate optional PSU presence, power and event evidence if the approved plan includes a state transition.
Identify missing mechanical observations while leaving the formal judgment to the engineer.
engineer_actions: Confirm safe PSU power/service state and physically actuate the specified handle/latch.
Observe fit, travel, engagement, release, retention and abnormal resistance.
Restore and verify the intended final mechanical state.
Apply the platform acceptance reference and set the formal testcase verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The explicit non-runnable marker matches the physical intent. It should not be converted into a BMC power command, PSU inventory read, or hot-swap sequence because none can prove handle accuracy and the source does not require electrical removal.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No command completes the test. If the approved plan intentionally changes PSU presence or power state, read-only BMC/PSU telemetry may be collected as supporting evidence only.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Attended Time 5 and Machine Time 20 are preserved as planning metadata. The source provides no repetition count, actuation force, electrical removal, hot-swap or runtime requirement.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a drawing-linked PSU handle/latch checklist with defined safe service state and photographs at open, engaged and restored positions. Add read-only PSU telemetry only when the approved plan includes an electrical state change.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected chassis, PSU FRU and bay design.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record chassis/PSU drawing and service-procedure revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Applicable platform mechanical drawing and approved PSU service procedure; no universal force or travel value is invented.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the latch/retention observations and safe power boundary explicit without changing the physical function under test.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: None for the handle/latch when all required positions and restoration are observed. PSU electrical behavior is outside scope unless the project explicitly adds it.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: PSU/bay identity, specification, safe service state and acceptance limits.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Photos cannot establish actuation force or retention strength, and telemetry cannot establish mechanical fit.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve a non-removal handle actuation or a controlled service/removal sequence according to its PSU architecture. The exact action and any electrical coverage must be recorded separately. A BMC presence reading does not substitute for handle/latch observation.
expected_evidence: Chassis, PSU FRU and bay identity plus drawing/service-procedure revision
Approved power/isolation and operator safety state
Photographs of initial, actuated/engaged, released and restored handle positions
Engineer checklist for alignment, travel, retention, release, free play, resistance, interference and damage
Optional PSU/BMC state and event deltas only if the plan includes a service-state transition
Safety-stop record and separately owned engineering verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The name, procedure and criterion all point to a physical PSU-handle accuracy check. The 5/20 timing difference is planning metadata under V3.1, and the vague word 'accuracy' requires a project specification rather than indicating contradictory source requirements.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The target and core manual operation are identifiable. Missing mechanical limits and safe power state are project inputs that gate execution; they do not make the Master row permanently impossible to review.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Accept the manual-only boundary and PSU-handle target; add the missing electrical-release, connector, pinch and evidence safeguards.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Keep V2's no-force, isolation, no-log-clear and operator-evidence improvements, while avoiding the unrequired assumption that the PSU must be removed.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates mechanical handle coverage from optional electrical PSU evidence and treats the timing fields and missing accuracy limits correctly as planning/readiness facts.

review_improvement: The revised contract defines what 'hardware accuracy' means for this PSU handle without inventing a hot-swap test. It adds the specific risk that actuation can release an energized supply and distinguishes supporting telemetry from the manual mechanical acceptance.
independent_technical_reasoning: A PSU handle is a load-bearing service and retention interface. Correct behavior depends on physical travel, latch engagement, release, alignment, resistance and final secure state, none of which a command or BMC sensor can establish. Because handle actuation may disengage a supply, the safe power architecture and service procedure must be known before execution. The source does not explicitly call for PSU removal or power interruption, so adding a hot-swap cycle would expand scope. The case is therefore MANUAL ONLY, readiness-gated by the PSU/bay specification, and not BLOCKED.

no_automatic_retry: A bind, failed latch, connector movement, unexpected power event or restoration problem ends the approved action. Preserve the physical state and evidence; do not automatically cycle the handle again or attempt an electrical recovery.
